rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Medinan; one view says it concerns Banū al-Naḍīr and counts it Medinan because they were near Medina.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مدنية. وقيل: نزلت في بني النضير، وتعد من المدينة لتدانيها منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū al-Naḍīr agreed to neutrality; after Badr they recognized Muhammad as the Torah’s prophet, but after Uḥud they doubted and broke the pact.
rows.anchor: وكان بنو النضير صالحوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، على أن لا يكونوا عليه ولا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ashraf allied with Quraysh; Gabriel informed the Prophet, who ordered Kaʿb killed by his milk-brother Muḥammad b. Maslama.
rows.anchor: فخرج كعب بن الأشرف في أربعين راكبا إلى مكة، فحالفوا عليه قريشا عند الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū al-Naḍīr had earlier plotted to drop a stone on the Prophet during his blood-money visit, but God protected him.
rows.anchor: فهموا بطرح الحجر على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فعصمه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Kaʿb’s death the Prophet ordered them out; they called for war, while another account says they requested ten days to prepare.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استمهلوه عشرة أيام ليتجهزوا للخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy’s faction urged them to stay, promising aid in battle or exile; they fortified alleys and plotted a dagger attack on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ودس المنافق عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه أن لا تخرجوا من الحصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim woman warned her brother of the plot, and he informed the Prophet before the Prophet reached them.
rows.anchor: فأخبرته بما أرادوا، فأسرع إلى الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام، فساره بخبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet besieged them for twenty-one nights; terror and loss of promised aid led them to seek peace, but he accepted only exile with limited baggage.
rows.anchor: فحاصرهم إحدى وعشرين ليلة، فقذف الله في قلوبهم الرعب وأيسوا من نصر المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went to Syria, Jericho, and Adhriʿāt; some went to Khaybar and al-Ḥīra, and captured arms included fifty coats, fifty helmets, and 340 swords.
rows.anchor: وقبض أموالهم وسلاحهم، فوجد خمسين درعا وخمسين بيضة وثلاثمائة وأربعين سيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ubayy promised two thousand followers and help from Qurayẓa and Ghatafān, but these allies deserted Banū al-Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: اعتزلتهم قريظة وخذلهم ابن أبي وحلفاؤهم من غطفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah follows the prior account of hypocrites and Jews allying by recounting God’s anger, the Jews’ exile, and His empowering the Prophet against those who plotted and allied with Quraysh.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها: أنه لما ذكر حال المنافقين واليهود وتولي بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are identified here as Qurayẓa, comparable to Banū al-Naḍīr; both clans were called al-Kāhinān and settled near Medina awaiting Muhammad.
rows.anchor: من أهل الكتاب: هم قريظة، وكانت قبيلة عظيمة توازن في القدر والمنزلة بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ديارهم attaches to أخرج; من أهل الكتاب completes an omitted predicate, and the possessive is apt because they built in an empty wilderness.
rows.anchor: من ديارهم: يتعلق بأخرج، ومن أهل الكتاب يتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لأول الحشر is temporal and attaches to أخرج; ḥashr means gathering people toward a destination.
rows.anchor: واللام في لأول الحشر تتعلق بأخرج، وهي لام التوقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most identify the expelled as Banū al-Naḍīr; al-Ḥasan says Qurayẓa, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects that because Qurayẓa were killed rather than exiled.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: إلى أن هؤلاء الذين أخرجوا هم بنو النضير. وقال الحسن: هم بنو قريظة ورد هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the first gathering the Prophet’s army assembling to fight them; a second could be ʿUmar’s gathering and exile of Khaybar’s people.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحشر هو حشر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الكتائب لقتالهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the first gathering as the beginning of Resurrection, with rising from the graves its later stage.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد حشر القيامة، أي هذا أوله، والقيام من القبور آخره

rows.speaker: عكرمة والزهري
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Zuhrī say the first gathering means the first gathering-place, Syria; another report says the Prophet directed Banū al-Naḍīr to the land of gathering.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والزهري: المعنى: الأول موضع الحشر، وهو الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies the later gathering with a fire driving people east to west; the early exile rule is now abrogated, leaving killing, captivity, or jizya.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجلاء كان في ابتداء الإسلام، وأما الآن فقد نسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers did not expect their departure because of their strength and forts; the Jews thought their fortifications would protect them from God.
rows.anchor: لعظم أمرهم ومنعتهم وقوتهم ووثاقة حصونهم وكثرة عددهم وعددهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says fronting the predicate highlights their trust in their forts, while making them the subject of أن depicts their self-image as invulnerable.
rows.anchor: في تقديم الخبر على المبتدأ دليل على فرط وثوقهم بحصانتها ومنعها إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers parsing حصونهم as the subject of مانعتهم rather than as a fronted nominal subject, avoiding disputed word order.
rows.anchor: بل الراجح أن يكون حصونهم فاعلة بمانعتهم

rows.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح وابن جريج
rows.claim: Al-Suddī, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and Ibn Jurayj explain God’s unexpected coming as the killing of leader Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf, weakening them.
rows.anchor: قاله السدي وأبو صالح وابن جريج، وذلك مما أضعف قوتهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Muslims damaged forts from outside to enter while the Jews destroyed homes from within.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: خرب المؤمنون من خارج ليدخلوا، وخربوا هم من داخل

rows.speaker: الضحاك والزجاج وغيرهما
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Zajjāj, and others say the Jews demolished houses whenever Muslims damaged the forts.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك والزجاج وغيرهما: كانوا كلما خرب المسلمون من حصونهم

rows.speaker: الزهري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī and others say they dismantled good timber after being allowed only what camels could carry; the siege prompted this, hence believers’ role is attributed.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري وغيره: كانوا، لما أبيح لهم ما تستقل به الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says they ruined houses out of stinginess, unwilling to leave them intact.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شحوا على بقائها سليمة، فخربوها إفسادا

rows.speaker: قتادة والجحدري ومجاهد وأبو حيوة وعيسى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers geminate يخربون; the remaining seven use the lighter form, and both readings convey the same causative meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة والجحدري ومجاهد وأبو حيوة وعيسى وأبو عمرو: يخربون مشددا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr b. al-ʿAlāʾ distinguishes خرب, to demolish or spoil, from أخرب, to leave a place ruined and depart.
rows.anchor: خرب بمعنى هدم وأفسد، وأخرب: ترك الموضع خرابا وذهب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اعتبروا means recognize God’s plan to expel them through believers without a full battle; another report says the Prophet promised Muslims their property without fighting.
rows.anchor: فاعتبروا: تفطنوا لما دبر الله من إخراجهم بتسليط المؤمنين عليهم من غير قتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the decree of exile, God would have punished them by killing and captivity; the respite could allow descendants to believe.
rows.anchor: لعذبهم في الدنيا بالقتل والسبي، كما فعل بإخوانهم بني قريظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tradition says Banū al-Naḍīr disobeyed Moses by sparing an Amalekite king’s son for his beauty; barred from Israel after Moses died, they settled in the Hijaz.
rows.anchor: وكان بنو النضير من الجيش الذين عصوا موسى في كونهم لم يقتلوا الغلام ابن ملك العماليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel’s decreed exile came upon them through Muhammad; otherwise they would have faced the sword as at Badr.
rows.anchor: وكان الله قد كتب على بني إسرائيل جلاء، فنالهم هذا الجلاء على يد محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One distinction says جلاء is exile with family, unlike إخراج, which may leave family behind; al-Māwardī says exile is collective but removal may be individual.
rows.anchor: قيل: والفرق بين الجلاء والإخراج: أن الجلاء ما كان مع الأهل والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read الجلاء long, al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ and ʿAlī b. Ṣāliḥ short, and Ṭalḥa with hamza; escape from worldly punishment does not avert the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: الجلاء ممدودا والحسن بن صالح وأخوه علي بن صالح: مقصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa reads ومن يشاقق with clear consonants; the majority assimilate them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: ومن يشاقق بالإظهار، كالمتفق عليه في الأنفال والجمهور بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Companions began cutting and burning Nadir palms; after the Jews objected, the palm verse affirmed God’s permission and the humiliation of the enemy.
rows.anchor: كان بعض الصحابة قد شرع في بعض نخل بني النضير يقطع ويحرق

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد وعمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Ibn Zayd, and ʿAmr b. Maymūn say līna and palm tree are synonymous.
rows.anchor: واللينة والنخلة اسمان بمعنى واحد، قاله الحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد وعمرو بن ميمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and linguists define līna as any palm other than ʿajwa; al-Thawrī says it is a choice palm.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وجماعة من أهل اللغة: هي النخلة ما لم تكن عجوة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وسفيان
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Sufyān identify it as a palm bearing a date type called al-lawn; Sufyān says the yellow fruit is translucent enough to reveal its pit.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وسفيان: ما ثمرها لون، وهو نوع من التمر يقال له اللون

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also says al-līn means mixed palms without ʿajwa or barnī; Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad says līna is ʿajwa.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا أبو عبيدة: اللين: ألوان النخل المختلطة التي ليس فيها عجوة ولا برني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other definitions are sayalān, soft tree branches, a short palm, or oleander; poems are cited as evidence for the word’s usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي السيلان، وأنشد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a conditional object of قطعتم, من لينة clarifies it, and the answer says cutting or leaving is by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: وما شرطية منصوبة بقطعتم، ومن لينة تبيين لإبهام ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read قائمة, agreeing with ما by meaning; other readers use قوما or masculine قائما, and أصلها is read without wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور قائمة، أنث قائمة، والضمير في تركتموها على معنى ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims asked to divide Nadir property as booty, but revelation calls it fayʾ: no cavalry or camels were deployed, no distance crossed, and only the Prophet rode.
rows.anchor: بين أن أموالهم فيء، لم يوجف عليها خيل ولا ركاب ولا قطعت مسافة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar says the property belonged exclusively to the Prophet, who spent a year’s family upkeep and used the balance for arms and cavalry.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب: كانت أموال بني النضير لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the Prophet gave it to the Emigrants, excepting three poor Anṣārī men who received shares.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كانت له عليه الصلاة والسلام، فآثر بها المهاجرين وقسمها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be conditional or relative; أفاء means “will return,” so a pre-exile revelation predicts the event, while a later one explains its ruling.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله: وما أفاء الله على رسوله شرطية أو موصولة، وأفاء بمعنى: يفيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من before خيل is additional and implies exhaustive scope; ركاب means camels. Some scholars say property gained without force belongs exclusively to rulers.
rows.anchor: ومن في: من خيل زائدة في المفعول يدل عليه الاستغراق، والركاب: الإبل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the second fayʾ statement has no conjunction because it explains the first and directs distribution like the fifth of war booty.
rows.anchor: لم يدخل العاطف على هذه الجملة، لأنها بيان للأولى، فهي منها غير أجنبية عنها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies the villages as al-Ṣafrāʾ, Yanbuʿ, Wādī al-Qurā, and nearby Arab villages; unlike Nadir property, none was retained by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أهل القرى المذكورون في هذه الآية هم أهل الصفراء وينبع ووادي القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view restricts the first verse to Nadir property and treats the next as general; most read يكون while some read تكون.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الآية الأولى خاصة في بني النضير، وهذه الآية عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary the vowels of دولة; ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar says the forms are synonymous, while al-Kisāʾī and Basran authorities distinguish rotation of property from ownership.
rows.anchor: قال عيسى بن عمر: هما بمعنى واحد. وقال الكسائي وحذاق البصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine تكون follows ما by meaning, property; masculine يكون follows its wording. دولة can be an accusative predicate or a nominative subject with complete يكون.
rows.anchor: والضمير في تكون بالتأنيث عائد على معنى ما، إذ المراد به الأموال والمغانم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distribution prevents property circulating only among the wealthy or being seized through pre-Islamic privilege by the strongest.
rows.anchor: كي لا يكون الفيء الذي حقه أن يعطى للفقراء بلغة يعيشون بها متداولا بين الأغنياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Anṣār sought shares from conquered villages; al-Kalbī says Muslim leaders asked the Prophet to take a choice and a quarter, leaving the rest as in pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: وروي أن قوما من الأنصار تكلموا في هذه القرى المفتتحة وقالوا: لنا منها سهمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to follow the Messenger applies generally to fayʾ and spoils; its generality was used to infer prohibitions of wine, tattooing, and sewn garments in consecration.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام يدخل فيه قسمة ما أفاء الله والغنائم وغيرها

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī answered a question about a consecrated pilgrim killing a hornet by citing the command to follow the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أن الشافعي، رحمه الله تعالى، قال: سلوني عما شئتم أخبركم به من كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa reports the Prophet’s instruction to follow Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; another report says ʿUmar ordered a consecrated pilgrim to kill a hornet.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة بن اليمان، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اقتدوا باللذين من بعدي أبي بكر وعمر»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes للفقراء an appositive to ذي القربى and its coordinate, not فلله وللرسول, saying the Messenger is too exalted to be called poor.
rows.anchor: للفقراء، قال الزمخشري: بدل من قوله: ولذي القربى، والمعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reflects the Ḥanafī view that relatives qualify only if poor; al-Shāfiʿī makes kinship itself the cause, so even wealthy relatives may receive.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعله الزمخشري بدلا من قوله: ولذي القربى، لأنه مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says للفقراء المهاجرين clarifies the needy and wayfarer categories and repeats the lām to distinguish them from the wealthy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: للفقراء المهاجرين بيان لقوله: والمساكين وابن السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Emigrants are truthful in their faith and striving, by word and deed.
rows.anchor: أولئك هم الصادقون: أي في إيمانهم وجهادهم قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates the settled Anṣār with Emigrants, making both groups recipients; another reading starts a sentence with يحبون as predicate.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: والذين تبوؤا معطوف على المهاجرين، وهم الأنصار

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī coordinates abode and faith as clauses: they settled in Medina and believed sincerely; other parses make تبوؤا imply adherence or faith a figurative dwelling.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو من عطف الجمل، أي واعتقدوا الإيمان وأخلصوا فيه، قاله أبو علي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains دار الإيمان as the House of Faith or a name for Medina where emigration and faith appeared.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو أراد دار الهجرة ودار الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says they settled in the abode together with faith, making “before them” coherent; من قبلهم means before migration and حاجة means envy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والمعنى تبوؤا الدار مع الإيمان معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to an Anṣārī who hosted the Prophet’s guest despite having only food for his children; the Prophet said God marveled at their action the previous night.
rows.anchor: قصة الأنصاري مع ضيف الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، حيث لم يكن لهم إلا ما يأكل الصبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خصاصة means poverty, likened to gaps between a house’s sticks.
rows.anchor: والخصاصة: الفاقة، مأخوذة من خصاص البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ is innate tightness about one’s possessions and eagerness to withhold; Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with kasra, unlike the majority.
rows.anchor: والشح: اللؤم، وهو كزازة النفس على ما عندها، والحرص على المنع

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line pictures a miserly soul resisting generosity; the verse about souls being brought face to face with stinginess is also linked.
rows.anchor: يمارس نفسا بين جنبيه كزة ... إذا هم بالمعروف قالت له مهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says paying required alms, hosting guests, and giving in hardship frees one from stinginess.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «من أدى الزكاة المفروضة وقرى الضيف وأعطى في النائبة فقد برىء من الشح»

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says those coming later are a third group of Companions; most exegetes say the Tābiʿūn. If coordinated with prior beneficiaries, they share in the fayʾ ruling.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: هم الفرقة الثالثة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another syntax makes later Muslims until the end of time a new group praised for praying for earlier believers; Mālik b. Aws recounts ʿUmar distinguishing charity, booty, and fayʾ, then including every Muslim.
rows.anchor: والذين جاؤ من بعدهم: الظاهر أنه معطوف على ما قبله من المعطوف على المهاجرين

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar says without future generations he would have divided every conquered village as the Prophet divided Khaybar.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه: لولا من يأتي من آخر الناس ما فتحت قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative syntax detaches later Muslims until Judgment as a new subject, praising their prayers and love for earlier believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: والذين جاؤ من بعدهم مقطوع مما قبله، معطوف عطف الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites’ assurances were revealed about ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy, Rifāʿa b. al-Tābūt, and hypocritical Anṣār who messaged Banū al-Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي، ورفاعة بن التابوت، وقوم من منافقي الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لإخوانهم marks transmission; their brotherhood is unbelief and alliance. ولا نطيع فيكم may concern fighting or abandoning their promise of support.
rows.anchor: واللام في لإخوانهم للتبليغ، والأخوة بينهم أخوة الكفر وموالاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لننصرنكم answers an implicit oath, while the conditional answer is omitted; failure to leave or assist the Jews demonstrates prophecy.
rows.anchor: ولننصرنكم: جواب قسم محذوف قبل إن الشرطية، وجواب إن محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers may be Banū al-Naḍīr or Jews of Medina; al-Zamakhsharī treats aid hypothetically, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya says breaking the promise would mean defeat.
rows.anchor: وهذا إذا كان قوله: لإخوانهم أنهم بنو النضير. وقيل: هم يهود المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the verbs answer the oath rather than condition; he gives the standard rule that the oath takes the answer and the conditional answer is omitted.
rows.anchor: لا يخرجون ولا ينصرون لأنها راجعة على حكم القسم، لا على حكم الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites fear believers more than God because they expect immediate human harm but, lacking faith, do not expect God’s later punishment.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يتوقعون عاجل شركم، ولعدم إيمانهم لا يتوقعون أجل عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رهبة is passive in sense: believers are the more feared; locating the verbal noun in their breasts shows how deeply fear is settled.
rows.anchor: رهبة: مصدر رهب المبني للمفعول، كأنه قيل: أشد مرهوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in صدورهم may refer to Jews, hypocrites, or both; a poem illustrates the passive sense of someone being feared.
rows.anchor: والضمير في صدورهم. قيل: لليهود، وقيل: للمنافقين، وقيل: للفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا يقاتلونكم may refer to Banū al-Naḍīr and all Jews or Jews with hypocrites; they fight only from fortified towns or behind walls.
rows.anchor: لا يقاتلونكم: أي بنو النضير وجميع اليهود. وقيل: اليهود والمنافقون جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary between جدر with two dammas, a softened form, جدار with alif, and a Yemeni جدر reading with fatḥa on jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: جدر بضمتين، جمع جدار وأبو رجاء والحسن وابن وثاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the people before them as Banū Qaynuqāʿ, expelled before Banū al-Naḍīr; another view means the unbelievers at Badr.
rows.anchor: وهم بنو قينقاع، أجلاهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من المدينة قبل بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies earlier hypocrites as hypocrites of past nations, defeated and disgraced; قريبا can instead mean punishment followed rebellion quickly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في من قبلهم للمنافقين، والذين من قبلهم: منافقو الأمم الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main parable makes hypocrites like Satan and Banū al-Naḍīr like the human whom Satan lures into sin then abandons, as hypocrites urged resistance and deserted them.
rows.anchor: فالمنافقون كالشيطان، وبنو النضير كالإنسان، والجمهور: على أن الشيطان والإنسان اسما جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings apply the parable to Satan seducing Quraysh at Badr or to a specific Satan who led a murderer to unbelief and then abandoned him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد استغواء الشيطان قريشا يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s claim that he fears God is mere display and does not prevent him from inducing evil.
rows.anchor: وقول الشيطان: إني أخاف الله رياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read عاقبتهما accusative while al-Ḥasan, ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd, and Sulaym b. Arqam read nominative; they also differ on خالدين and predicate structure.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: عاقبتهما بنصب التاء والحسن وعمرو بن عبيد وسليم بن أرقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing hypocrites and Jews, God admonishes believers; admonition after calamity affects softened hearts and warns against causes of punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما انقضى في هذه السورة، وصف المنافقين واليهود. وعظ المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God either reinforces the first or distinguishes performing obligations from avoiding sins under threat.
rows.anchor: وكرر الأمر بالتقوى على سبيل التوكيد، أو لاختلاف متعلق بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read ولتنظر as an imperative; several read the lām with kasra, and al-Ḥasan makes it a purpose lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ولتنظر: أمرا، واللام ساكنة وأبو حيوة ويحيى بن الحارث: بكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The certain Resurrection is called tomorrow to bring it near; other views make tomorrow the afterlife or day of death, and Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say yesterday is this world.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أمر القيامة كائنا لا محالة، عبر عنه بالغد، وهو اليوم الذي يلي يومك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the indefinite نفس stresses each soul’s need to consider what it sent ahead for a tremendous, unknowable tomorrow.
rows.anchor: أما تنكير النفس فاستقلال للأنفس النواظر فيما قدمن للآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says those who forgot God are disbelievers who neglected worship and obedience, then desires made them fail to save themselves; this matches sin with punishment.
rows.anchor: وتركوا عبادة الله وامتثال ما أمر واجتناب ما نهى، وهذا تنبيه على فرط غفلتهم

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān explains forgetting themselves as losing sight of their own interests.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان: المعنى حظ أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Fire and Paradise are not alike; the author links this to verses distinguishing believers from sinners and the mindful from the wicked.
rows.anchor: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain verse is a figurative parable, like the trust presented to the heavens, reproaching humans for hard hearts that fail to respond to revelation.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب التخييل والتمثيل، كما مر في قوله تعالى: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa assimilates tāʾ into ṣād in his reading مصدعا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: مصدعا، بإدغام التاء في الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Samāl and Abū Dīnār read al-Quddūs with fatḥa; most use ḍamma. Most read المؤمن with kasra, while Abū Jaʿfar reads it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: المؤمن بكسر الميم، اسم فاعل من آمن بمعنى أمن

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects the fatḥa reading as requiring an omitted preposition; al-Zamakhsharī defends it by positing that omission.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: لا يجوز ذلك، لأنه لو كان كذلك لكان المؤمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muhaymin was explained earlier; al-Jabbār means overpowering, unreachable, majestic per Ibn ʿAbbās, or one who repairs broken things.
rows.anchor: الجبار: القهار الذي جبر خلقه على ما أراد. وقيل: الجبار: الذي لا يدانيه شيء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives jabbār from compelling someone and knows no فعال form from أفعل except jabbār and darrāk; Abū Ḥayyān adds usār.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: من أجبره على الأمر: قهره، قال: ولم أسمع فعالا من أفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir is immense in greatness or exalted above wronging servants; the Creator determines, al-Bāriʾ differentiates forms, and al-Muṣawwir shapes them.
rows.anchor: المتكبر: المبالغ في الكبرياء والعظمة. وقيل: المتكبر عن ظلم عباده

rows.speaker: علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السميقع
rows.claim: ʿAlī, Ḥāṭib, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read المصور with fatḥa on wāw and rāʾ, as an object of al-Bāriʾ referring to things fashioned.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السميقع: المصور بفتح الواو والراء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī also reads wāw with fatḥa and rāʾ with kasra, making the active participle annexed to its object.
rows.anchor: وعن علي فتح الواو وكسر الراء على إضافة اسم الفاعل إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body and wood are familiar; اسندت ظهري إلى الحائط means leaning against a wall, while تساند القوم means people aligning face to face for battle.
rows.anchor: الجسم والخشب معروفان. أسندت ظهري إلى الحائط: أملته وأضفته إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Medinan and was revealed during the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq expedition in response to statements by ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy and his followers.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مدنية، نزلت في غزوة بني المصطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A water dispute led to calls for Anṣār and Emigrants; Ibn Ubayy attacked funding the Prophet’s followers and boasted the strongest would expel the weakest. Zayd b. Arqam reported it; revelation confirmed Zayd and exposed Ibn Ubayy.
rows.anchor: فسمعه زيد بن أرقم، ونقل ذلك إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior sermon dispersal happened as believers rushed to a provision caravan during famine; the surah then exposes wealthy hypocrites’ hostility toward poor Emigrants who left property and trade for God.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها: أنه لما كان سبب الانفضاض عن سماع الخطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read تسمع with second-person address; ʿIkrima and ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī use passive يسمع, with قولهم as subject because the verb means to attend or incline, not via an extra lām.
rows.anchor: تسمع بتاء الخطاب وعكرمة وعطية العوفي: يسمع بالياء مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble propped logs because their minds lack faith; logs leaning on walls are useless, or they resemble idols; the comparison can be independent or circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وشبهوا بالخشب لعزوب أفهامهم وفراغ قلوبهم من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary the vocalization of خشب; one view makes it the plural of hollow rotten wood to match corrupt interiors, while Ibn al-Musayyab and Ibn Jubayr read a collective noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: خشب بضم الخاء والشين والبراء بن عازب والنحويان وابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are bodies without souls or minds; handsome, eloquent examples include ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy, al-Jadd b. Qays, and Muʿattib b. Qushayr.
rows.anchor: أشباح بلا أرواح، وأجسام بلا أحلام. وذكر ممن كان ذا بهاء وفصاحة عبد الله بن أبي

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poem warns against judging by beards and appearances, likening most people to cattle or fruitless clouds and branches.
rows.anchor: لا تخدعنك اللحى ولا الصور ... تسعة أعشار من ترى بقر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says shouts, lost-animal announcements, or news of revelation frightened them because they feared their lives and property could become lawful.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: كانوا متى سمعوا بنشدان ضالة أو صياحا بأي وجه كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem illustrates panic; Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes it to Jarīr and al-Zamakhsharī to al-Akhṭal. Al-Zamakhsharī permits parsing هم العدو as a second object.
rows.anchor: أنشده ابن عطية لجرير، ونسب هذا البيت الزمخشري للأخطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects هم العدو as a second object; it naturally declares hypocrites true enemies, explaining the order to beware them.
rows.anchor: بل المتبادر إلى الذهن السليم أن يكون هم العدو إخبارا منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قاتلهم الله is a curse and rebuke, also used to express amazement; أنى يؤفكون means how they turn from truth, not a bare adverb modifying the curse.
rows.anchor: وقاتلهم الله: كلمة ذم وتوبيخ، وقالت العرب: قاتله الله ما أشعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God vindicated Zayd, Ibn Ubayy refused advice to seek pardon, mockingly saying they had already urged him to believe and pay alms and might as well order worship of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال له بعضهم: امض إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واعترف بذنبك يستغفر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s seeking forgiveness entails their repentance from hypocrisy, but they persist in turning away arrogantly.
rows.anchor: واستغفار الرسول لهم، هو استتابتهم من النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Nāfiʿ, and Medinans read لووا with light wāw; Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash, and others geminate it for repetition or intensity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ونافع وأهل المدينة وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense يصدون is circumstantial and signals persistence; وهم مستكبرون is another circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: يصدون ويصدون، جملة حالية، وأتت بالمضارع ليدل على استمرارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God knew they would never believe, seeking forgiveness and not seeking it are equal; Makkī says the Prophet sought it because they outwardly professed Islam.
rows.anchor: ولما سبق في علمه تعالى أنهم لا يؤمنون البتة، سوى بين استغفاره لهم وعدمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this followed the verse in al-Tawba about seeking forgiveness seventy times and the Prophet’s promise to exceed seventy, ending any basis for more requests.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت هذه بعد قوله تعالى في براءة إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read أستغفرت with the equalizing hamza; Abū Jaʿfar lengthens it. The wording is declarative but means an interrogative, and أم signals the omitted hamza.
rows.anchor: واللفظ خبر، والمعنى على الاستفهام، والمراد التسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preceding exchange ends with affirmation that might belongs to God, His Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: قال: نعم، فقال: أشهد أن العزة لله ولرسوله وللمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Money distracts through pursuit of increase and enjoyment of accumulation; children distract through delight and concern for their interests. Remembrance broadly includes prayer, praise, glorification, and supplication.
rows.anchor: لا تلهكم أموالكم بالسعي في نمائها والتلذذ بجمعها، ولا أولادكم بسروركم بهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك وعطاء
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ restrict remembrance to obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan also says all duties, al-Kalbī says jihad with the Messenger, and another view says Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وعطاء: أكد هنا الصلاة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those distracted by wealth and children lose by choosing the immediate over the later and the perishable over the lasting.
rows.anchor: حيث آثروا العاجل على الآجل، والفاني على الباقي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most interpret spending as zakat; another view includes required and voluntary charity. Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerns those withholding alms and addresses believers.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: المراد الزكاة. وقيل: عام في المفروض والمندوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لولا أخرتني means “why did You not delay me?” briefly so the dying person can give charity and become righteous.
rows.anchor: لولا أخرتني: أي هلا أخرت موتي إلى زمان قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read فأصدق in the subjunctive after the wish; some read فأتصدق. Most make وأكن jussive, while al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya coordinate it with فأصدق by position.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فأصدق، وهو منصوب على جواب الرغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordination by position has an absent governor with a remaining syntactic position; coordination by supposition has an absent governor with its effect remaining.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين العطف على الموضع والعطف على التوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several readers use subjunctive وأكون; ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr reads it independently as a promise of righteousness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير: وأكون بضم النون على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God will not delay a soul when its term arrives urges haste in obedience before death comes without preparation.
rows.anchor: فيه تحريض على المبادرة بأعمال الطاعات حذارا أن يجيء الأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read تعملون addressing everyone; Abū Bakr reads third person as a threat to unbelievers, perhaps still general.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تعملون بتاء الخطاب، للناس كلهم وأبو بكر: بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghābun derives from loss-making but is not reciprocal between two parties here; it is one-sided, like tawāḍaʿa and taḥāmala.
rows.anchor: التغابن: تفاعل من الغبن وليس من اثنين، بل هو من واحد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Prophet said God created Pharaoh an unbeliever in the womb; Yaḥyā b. Zakariyyā related the contrary, that he was a believer there.
rows.anchor: روى ابن مسعود أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: «خلق الله فرعون في البطن كافرا»

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says some disbelieve in God while believing in stars, and others believe in God while disbelieving in stars.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء بن أبي رباح: فمنكم كافر بالله، مؤمن بالكواكب ومؤمن بالله وكافر بالكوكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers are named first because more numerous, supported by verses saying only a few of God’s servants are grateful or righteous.
rows.anchor: وقدم الكافر لكثرته. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى: وقليل من عبادي الشكور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads disbelief and faith as human choices and acts; God sees these, and creation should prompt reflection and gratitude. Abū Ḥayyān calls this Muʿtazilite doctrine.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فمنكم آت بالكفر وفاعل له، ومنكم آت بالإيمان وفاعل له

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Another view from al-Zamakhsharī says unbelievers are materialists who reject creation, contrasted with believers in creation; Abū Ḥayyān suspects the Muʿtazila falsely attributed a missing “sinner” view to al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا: وقيل: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر بالخلق: هم الدهرية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says fronting له الملك وله الحمد restricts true sovereignty and praise to God, source and sustainer of all; others’ rule and praise are derivative.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ليدل بتقدمهما على معنى اختصاص الملك والحمد بالله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read صوركم with ḍamma on ṣād; Zayd b. ʿAlī and Abū Razīn use kasra. Human form is a bodily blessing of abilities and beauty, or rational perception and its capacities.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: صوركم بضم الصاد وزيد بن علي وأبو رزين. بكسرها
